response_change.parent_relation: With fixed Kd, theta_bound increases hyperbolically with L as L/(Kd+L), giving one shared half-saturation threshold and a Hill-slope-like shape fixed by independent identical sites.
response_change.child_relation: Release the assumption that all sites are equivalent by allowing a heterogeneous population of binding affinities across enzyme molecules or microstates, so the observed theta_bound versus L becomes a broader non-Langmuir binding isotherm with altered low-L and mid-range curvature even though saturation still approaches 1.
response_change.observable_effect: Across ligand titrations at fixed temperature, enzyme abundance, and mixing, the occupancy curve becomes systematically broader around half-saturation than the parent hyperbola; a single refitted Kd cannot simultaneously match both the initial rise and the approach to saturation over that range.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when ligand concentrations span below and above the nominal dissociation scale, especially L on the order of Kd to a few-fold around it, and when affinity heterogeneity is not negligible compared with the mean Kd.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as a modest broadening of the binding curve over sampled L near Kd; in holdout, the same heterogeneous-affinity mechanism extends to more pronounced mismatch between low-L slope and upper-tail saturation if the L range is widened.
plan.continuation_path: As the affinity distribution narrows to a delta function around one Kd, the heterogeneous model continuously recovers theta_bound = L/(Kd+L).
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes one perfectly uniform binding affinity, omitting realistic static heterogeneity in effective dissociation strengths across enzyme conformers or microenvironments.
plan.baseline_assumption: All binding sites are independent and equivalent.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Quenched heterogeneity in effective binding affinity produces an ensemble-averaged occupancy curve that is broader than a single-site Langmuir isotherm.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: at fixed Kd the map from free ligand concentration L to theta_bound is a one-threshold hyperbola with fixed curvature and half-saturation exactly at L=Kd. Proposed refinement: relax equivalence of sites while keeping rapid reversible equilibrium and independent occupancy, so the scored target mapping itself changes from a single Langmuir curve to an ensemble-averaged isotherm with broader transition shape. Varied condition: L is titrated over a range spanning sub-Kd to supra-Kd values; held fixed: temperature, enzyme abundance, mixing, and the structural stability assumption. Concrete contrast: if the true system has appreciable affinity heterogeneity, then relative to the parent, occupancy can rise more gradually through the midrange while still approaching saturation near 1 at high L. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both that broadened midrange curvature and the corresponding low-L behavior, because refitting Kd only shifts the same hyperbolic shape along the L axis without changing its normalized shape. This is scientifically admissible when the measured enzyme pool contains multiple persistent microstates or local environments during the assay. Limitation: if heterogeneity is very small or the observed L range is too narrow around one side of Kd, the parent may remain an adequate approximation.

contract.assumption_after: Binding remains independent and at equilibrium, but the enzyme population contains persistent heterogeneity in effective dissociation strengths across molecules or microstates.
contract.observable_signature: Parent response relationship: a one-threshold hyperbola with half-saturation fixed by Kd and fixed curvature under ligand titration. contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting the parent while ignoring heterogeneity leaves only the single-threshold Langmuir shape L/(Kd + L), which can shift the half-saturation location through Kd but cannot change the normalized curvature. Here the heterogeneous mechanism makes the effective denominator grow as Kd*sqrt(1 + heterogeneity_width*L/Kd), so one shared parent parameter set cannot simultaneously match both the low-L rise and the broadened midrange-to-upper approach across the stated ligand range.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed heterogeneity_width, theta_bound is a one-parameter monotone isotherm in the ratio L/Kd, so changing Kd only rescales the concentration axis while preserving the same broadening rule.
response_change.child_relation: Introduce an environmental modulation of the heterogeneity broadening so the effect of affinity scale Kd on theta_bound is not just a horizontal rescaling: the apparent width of the occupancy transition changes with the sampled binding-strength condition.
response_change.observable_effect: Across datasets where both ligand concentration and effective binding strength vary, low- and mid-occupancy slopes differ systematically between weak- and strong-binding conditions, not just by a shift in the concentration axis.

plan.activation_condition: Most visible when heterogeneity_width is appreciable and measurements span comparable values of L and Kd so that L/Kd is O(1); if heterogeneity_width≈0 or only one Kd condition is sampled, the extra interaction is weak or unidentifiable.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, variation over L and Kd already tests whether curves at different Kd collapse by a single rescaling; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to more extreme Kd where the change in transition broadness with binding strength becomes clearer.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the new modulation strength tends to zero, so heterogeneity broadening becomes independent of the binding-strength condition.
plan.promotion_reason: The current inputs cannot represent the fixed but omitted environmental condition that can alter the spread of static affinities across enzyme microstates. A new independently sampled static input is needed to expose a non-separable interaction rather than merely refitting constants.
plan.gap_statement: The parent treats static affinity heterogeneity as having a fixed width across all experimental conditions, although solvent composition or crowding can change the breadth of microstate affinities without changing the one-site reversible-binding mechanism.
plan.baseline_assumption: heterogeneity_width is constant and condition-independent across all measurements.
plan.scientific_mechanism: A controlled environmental condition such as cosolvent or crowding level changes the distribution width of effective binding affinities, so ensemble broadening itself varies across experiments.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with temperature, enzyme abundance, and mixing fixed, theta_bound depends on L and Kd through a single broadened occupancy curve governed by one shared heterogeneity_width, so changing Kd mainly shifts the concentration scale. Child change: allow an omitted sampled condition to modulate the heterogeneity breadth, creating a genuine interaction in the target mapping where the slope and curvature of theta_bound versus L depend on both affinity scale and environment. Distinguishing condition: vary ligand concentration L and effective binding strength Kd across measurements while holding the new environmental condition fixed at different sampled levels; then compare mid-occupancy regions. The child predicts that curves at different environmental levels cannot all be collapsed by one shared parent parameter set because the transition broadness changes, not only its horizontal location. This is scientifically admissible when microstate heterogeneity is substantial and the environment is known to alter conformational or solvation diversity, but it may be weak if heterogeneity is near zero or the sampled Kd range is too narrow.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps ligand concentration to occupancy through one effective broadened threshold set by Kd and a crowding-dependent heterogeneity width, yielding a single smoothly broadened monotone binding curve at each crowding level.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the symmetric square-root broadening assumption with a skew-capable affinity-distribution effect so that the low-L shoulder and high-L saturation approach can change differently as crowding varies, creating crowding-dependent curvature beyond a single broadened threshold.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed Kd, two experiments with different crowding_level can show similar midpoint occupancy but different early-rise versus late-saturation shape; the parent can only shift one common broadening scale and cannot independently alter both shoulders with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: Most visible when heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level) is order 0.1 to 10 and L/Kd spans sub-Kd to super-Kd values; if heterogeneity is near zero or crowding modulation is negligible, the extra curvature is not identifiable.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate crowding can already reveal broader versus sharper rises; in holdout, stronger crowding extends this into asymmetric low-L shoulder versus high-L tail behavior, exposing failure of a single-threshold broadening law.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added skew/non-symmetric correction tends to zero, or in the narrow-distribution limit heterogeneity_width -> 0.
plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes the affinity heterogeneity enters occupancy through one symmetric broadening form, which forces the same mathematical distortion on the onset and saturation sides of the binding curve.
plan.baseline_assumption: Static affinity heterogeneity is effectively symmetric and fully summarized by one width parameter entering a square-root denominator correction.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Crowding can not only widen but also skew the ensemble of microstate affinities, for example by preferentially stabilizing a subset of higher- or lower-affinity conformers, altering isotherm curvature without introducing kinetics or site coupling.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's symmetric-broadening assumption rather than add a wholly new process. The varied conditions are ligand concentration L and crowding_level, with temperature, enzyme abundance, and mixing still fixed and the measurement remaining an equilibrium occupancy. In the parent, crowding changes only one effective broadening scale, so once Kd, heterogeneity_width, and environment_modulation are globally fit, each crowding condition is constrained to the same family of curves with one shared onset-to-saturation shape. A scientifically plausible child allows crowding to skew the static affinity distribution, which changes curvature of theta_bound versus L: one crowding condition may show an extended low-concentration shoulder with relatively normal saturation, while another may preserve the midpoint but approach saturation more gradually. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because theta_bound(L,crowding_level) itself changes shape. The contrast is observable when the environment-modulated heterogeneity is non-negligible and L samples both below and above Kd; if heterogeneity is tiny, the refinement collapses back toward the parent and may be weakly identifiable.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when crowding_level is varied over a range large enough that crowding changes not only distribution breadth but also the central affinity, especially around L of order Kd where midpoint shifts are experimentally resolvable; weak or negligible if crowding mainly affects width and not mean affinity.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, crowding-dependent broadening may already be visible through slope differences at moderate L/Kd; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to conditions where curves at different crowding also separate by horizontal midpoint location, not just by steepness.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of zero crowding-induced shift of the central affinity, so crowding affects only width/skew and Kd remains the common center.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the environment changes only the spread and asymmetry of static affinities, but not the ensemble's central binding strength.
plan.baseline_assumption: Kd is a fixed central dissociation concentration independent of crowding_level.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Crowding or cosolvent can stabilize the bound or unbound conformational ensemble on average, shifting the mean effective affinity while simultaneously broadening and skewing the static distribution.
plan.rationale: Varied condition: crowding_level. Held fixed: temperature, enzyme abundance, mixing, and the static-equilibrium setting. Parent response: crowding changes the denominator only through heterogeneity broadening/skew terms built around the same central Kd, so any contrast across crowding is expressed as slope/curvature distortion around a fixed transition scale. Proposed child response: crowding also shifts the central affinity, producing a crowding-dependent threshold surface in the (L, crowding_level) plane. Concrete contrast: if higher crowding both broadens the curve and increases affinity, the occupancy rise occurs at lower L while also changing steepness; with one shared parent parameter set, widening/skewing alone cannot reproduce a consistent horizontal shift of the whole transition across multiple crowding conditions because Kd is fixed globally. This is scientifically admissible when crowding perturbs average solvation or conformer populations, not merely variance. Limitation: if experiments span only a narrow crowding range or midpoint locations are not resolved, the added mechanism may be weak and difficult to distinguish.

plan.scientific_mechanism: In disordered enzyme ensembles, additional crowding can broaden microstate populations faster than it keeps shifting the ensemble-mean affinity; once disorder is substantial, opposite microstate contributions partly cancel further mean-affinity motion, causing saturation of the threshold shift while broadening continues.

The effect is scientifically admissible when disorder becomes appreciable; it is weak in the limits L much less than Kd_eff or L much greater than Kd_eff because occupancy is already near 0 or 1. contract.activation_condition: Observable when crowding_level is varied over a range where w_env changes from small to order-one or larger, and ligand concentration is near the binding midpoint so threshold shifts alter theta_bound appreciably rather than being hidden in the low- or high-saturation limits.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate crowding already shows broadening and threshold movement; in holdout at higher crowding or larger heterogeneity_width, the child predicts diminishing additional threshold shift rather than the parent's continued same-form shift, producing a changed occupancy-crowding curvature with one shared parameter set.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the new saturation control tends to zero or when heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level) is small so the crowding shift reduces to the current form.
contract.domain_mechanism: saturating crowding-induced mean-affinity shift in a disordered binding ensemble
contract.scientific_mechanism: In disordered enzyme ensembles, additional crowding can broaden microstate populations faster than it keeps shifting the ensemble-mean affinity; once disorder is substantial, opposite microstate contributions partly cancel further mean-affinity motion, causing saturation of the threshold shift while broadening continues.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the new parameter acts jointly on crowding and heterogeneity amplitude inside the exponent denominator, changing the shape of threshold motion across crowding rather than simply rescaling its magnitude everywhere.
contract.assumption_before: Crowding changes the ensemble's central effective dissociation scale through a single unsaturating functional dependence on the same heterogeneity factor that broadens the curve.
contract.assumption_after: The crowding-induced mean-affinity shift saturates as the crowding-amplified heterogeneity amplitude grows, while the broadening and skew terms retain their original disorder dependence.
contract.before_fragment: L/(L + Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/(1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)))*sqrt(1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)*L/(Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/(1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)))) + skew_coupling*(heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)*L/(Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/(1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)))))**2/(1 + L/(Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/(1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)))))))
contract.after_fragment: L/(L + Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/((1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))*(1 + shift_saturation_strength*heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))))*sqrt(1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)*L/(Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/((1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))*(1 + shift_saturation_strength*heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))))) + skew_coupling*(heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level)*L/(Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/((1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))*(1 + shift_saturation_strength*heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))))))**2/(1 + L/(Kd*exp(-affinity_shift_coupling*crowding_level/((1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))*(1 + shift_saturation_strength*heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level))))))))
contract.parent_reduction: Set shift_saturation_strength = 0 to recover the parent exactly.
contract.observable_signature: With Kd, heterogeneity_width, environment_modulation, and skew_coupling fixed, varying crowding_level at ligand concentrations near the midpoint gives an occupancy curve whose initial crowding sensitivity remains parent-like but whose additional midpoint shift weakens at larger w_env; broadening still accumulates, so the mapping theta_bound(L,crowding_level) shows reduced high-crowding threshold motion rather than a uniform rescaling.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both the low-crowding steep threshold displacement and the high-crowding diminished incremental shift across the same crowding sweep, because in the parent the exponent curvature is locked to 1 + heterogeneity_width*(1 + environment_modulation*crowding_level). Changing affinity_shift_coupling, heterogeneity_width, or environment_modulation only rescales or retimes that fixed-form dependence, whereas the child introduces a second disorder-dependent damping of the mean shift without simultaneously suppressing the broadening term.
